被告被控二级谋杀罪，该司法管辖区采用 M'Naghten 测试。州法规将二级谋杀定义为普通法谋杀 (common-law murder)。
被告针对这项指控的最佳辩护是什么？

zh-choices.A: 非自愿醉酒 (Involuntary intoxication)。
zh-choices.B: 精神错乱 (Insanity)。
zh-choices.C: 无预谋恶意 (No malice aforethought)。
zh-choices.D: 无预谋 (No premeditation)。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Responsibility

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：在采用 M'Naghten 规则（M'Naghten test） 的州，精神疾病是否让被告不知道自己在做什么或不知道行为是错的，所以最强抗辩是 精神失常（insanity）。

三秒认题路径：

精神病幻觉 → 不知错 → M'Naghten → 不是自愿醉酒 → 选 insanity

核心法律规则

精神失常抗辩（insanity defense）在 M'Naghten test 下，考的是精神疾病有没有让被告无法理解行为的性质和后果（understanding nature and quality），或者无法知道行为是错的（knowing wrongfulness）。考场意思：只要题干能看出她因为幻觉真心觉得“这样做是对的”，就已经打中规则。

这里不是在比谁更疯，而是在看她当时能不能分辨“我在杀人”以及“这件事是错的”。题目说她相信幻觉女人的话是对的，所以最稳的结论是 insanity。

核心判例： M'Naghten 规则把重点锁在“知不知道自己在干什么、知不知道对错”，所以本题直接落到精神失常抗辩。

思维导图

先看被告能不能用精神失常挡住定罪？
关卡 1：题干有没有 mental illness？有，长期幻觉。
关卡 2：她是否在发作时知道自己在杀人，并且知道这事是错的？题干说她真信幻觉女人的话是对的。
关卡 3：卡死点：在 M'Naghten 下，“不知道对错”就够了，不用证明她完全失去控制。
结论：走 insanity，而不是去拼醉酒、杀人级别或是否预谋。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她一直自我用药、案发前又很醉，所以是不是 involuntary intoxication（非自愿醉酒）？

但考试真正问的是：真正让她动手的，是幻觉导致的精神疾病，不是被别人强行灌药。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。（本题对应地说，就是看有没有符合法律上的精神失常标准，不是看故事有多吓人。）

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干幻觉命令她杀人，且她真信那样做是对的，正好命中 M'Naghten 的“不知错”标准，所以最佳抗辩是 insanity。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 她是自己长期用药，不是被强行灌药，别把 involuntary intoxication 硬套上来。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ C: 她当时确有杀人故意，所以不能用“没有 malice aforethought”来洗掉罪名。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ D: 题目只考二级谋杀，不需要纠缠 premeditation 这个一级谋杀要件。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看精神状态抗辩，再排除醉酒与谋杀级别的偷换概念。

考场速记

记住一句：M'Naghten 只问两件事，知不知道自己在干什么，知不知道这样是错的。一看到幻觉、命令、真心以为“这是对的”，优先想 insanity，不要先被 intoxication 带跑。

reason.en: Acts as evidence of a severe mental illness.
reason.zh: 作为严重精神疾病之证据。

reason.en: Introduces facts that might tempt the test-taker to choose an intoxication defense.
reason.zh: 引入可能诱导考生选择醉酒抗辩的事实。

reason.en: Identifies the specific rule governing the insanity defense.
reason.zh: 确定规制精神失常抗辩的特定规则。

reason.en: Specifies the charge which the defense must defeat.
reason.zh: 指定了辩护方必须击败的指控罪名。

reason.en: Incorrect because the defendant voluntarily self-medicated.
reason.zh: 错误选项，因为被告人是自愿自我服药。

reason.en: Correct because her illness made her unable to know the wrongfulness of her act.
reason.zh: 正确选项，因为她的疾病使她无法认知行为的违法性。

reason.en: Incorrect because she intended to kill, satisfying malice aforethought.
reason.zh: 错误选项，因为她具有杀人意图，满足了恶意要件。

reason.en: Incorrect because second-degree murder at common law does not require premeditation.
reason.zh: 错误选项，因为普通法上的二级谋杀不需要预谋。

highlights.text: had visions of an unknown woman

reason.en: Establishes the presence of a mental disease or defect.
reason.zh: 确立了精神疾病或缺陷的存在。

highlights.text: truly believed that the unknown woman had her best interests at heart and that, therefore, whatever the woman said to do was right

reason.en: Directly satisfies the M'Naghten standard by showing she believed her actions were morally right.
reason.zh: 通过表明她相信自己的行为在道德上是正确的，直接满足麦纳顿测验标准。

highlights.text: history of self-medicating with drugs and alcohol

reason.en: Defeats any potential involuntary intoxication defense.
reason.zh: 击败任何潜在的非自愿醉酒抗辩。

highlights.text: uses the M'Naghten test

reason.en: Commands the application of the M'Naghten test rather than other insanity formulations.
reason.zh: 指令适用麦纳顿测验，而非其他精神失常标准公式。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
One evening, a man had several drinks and then started to drive home. As he was proceeding down Main Boulevard, an automobile pulled out of a side street to his right. The man's car struck this automobile broadside. The driver of the other car was killed as a result of the collision. A breath-analysis test administered after the accident showed that the man satisfied the legal definition of intoxication.
If the man is prosecuted for manslaughter, which of the following arguments would give him the best chance for acquittal?

choices.A: Because of his intoxication, the man lacked the mens rea needed for manslaughter.
choices.B: Driving while intoxicated requires no mens rea and therefore cannot be the basis for misdemeanor manslaughter.
choices.C: The collision would have occurred even if the man had not been intoxicated.
choices.D: The other driver was contributorily negligent.

questions.explanation:
Criminal causation
Actual (factual)
cause
  • Single cause – but for defendant's conduct, crime would not have occurred
  • Multiple causes – defendant's conduct was substantial factor causing crime
Proximate (legal)
cause
  • Crime was natural, probable & foreseeable consequence of defendant's conduct

There are two types of manslaughter:

  • Voluntary – an intentional killing mitigated by adequate provocation (ie, heat of passion) or, in some jurisdictions, other mitigating factors (eg, imperfect self-defense)
  • Involuntary – an unintentional killing that is caused by criminal negligence or occurs during the commission of an unlawful act (eg, misdemeanor manslaughter)

But to be convicted of manslaughter, the defendant's conduct must be the actual (ie, but for) cause and proximate (ie, foreseeable) cause of the specified result—the victim's death.

Here, the man's car struck a driver's vehicle, and the driver died as a result of the collision. The man would likely be charged with involuntary manslaughter since the collision occurred when he was driving under the influence of alcohol. But his unlawful act would not be the actual cause of the driver's death if the collision would have occurred even if the man had not been intoxicated. And since actual causation is required for a manslaughter conviction, this is the man's strong argument for acquittal.

(Choice A) Voluntary intoxication is a defense to a specific intent crime if the intoxication negated the requisite mens rea. But it is no defense to lesser intent crimes—eg, involuntary manslaughter stemming from criminal negligence (as seen here).

(Choice B) Any criminal act that is malum in se (ie, inherently wrong)—including driving while intoxicated—can serve as a basis for misdemeanor manslaughter, even if the criminal act requires no mens rea.

(Choice D) Even if the driver's negligence contributed to his death, the man could still be convicted of manslaughter if his drunk driving was a substantial factor in causing that death.

📌 Educational Objective

Crimes that require a specific result (eg, homicide) require proof that the defendant's conduct was both the actual (ie, but for) and proximate (ie, foreseeable) cause of that result.
questions.zh-question:
一天晚上，一名男子喝了几杯酒后开始开车回家。当他沿着 Main Boulevard 行驶时，一辆汽车从他右边的辅路驶出。该男子的车撞上了这辆车的侧面。另一辆车的司机因这次碰撞而死亡。事故后进行的呼吸分析测试显示，该男子符合醉酒的法律定义。

如果该男子被以过失杀人罪（manslaughter）起诉，以下哪项论点能让他有最大的机会被判无罪？

zh-choices.A: 由于醉酒，该男子缺乏构成过失杀人罪（manslaughter）所需的犯罪意图（mens rea）。
zh-choices.B: 醉酒驾驶不需要犯罪意图（mens rea），因此不能作为轻罪过失杀人罪（misdemeanor manslaughter）的基础。
zh-choices.C: 即使该男子没有醉酒，碰撞也同样会发生。
zh-choices.D: 另一名司机存在与有过失。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Definition

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：非故意杀人（manslaughter）里，酒驾虽然违法，但还得证明它是死亡的事实原因（actual cause）和近因（proximate cause），少一个都不行。

三秒认题路径：

酒后驾车 → 人死了 → 先看原因 → 再看近因 → 选 C

核心法律规则

非故意杀人（involuntary manslaughter）通常指因刑事过失（criminal negligence）或违法行为（unlawful act）造成死亡。考场上最关键的是：被告行为必须同时是事实原因（actual cause），也就是“如果没有这行为，死者还会不会死”，以及近因（proximate cause），也就是死亡是不是该行为的可预见结果。

本题里，酒驾只是背景，真正卡点是：如果碰撞“即使没醉也会发生”，那就缺了but for causation，被告就很有力地主张无罪。

核心判例： 无需特定判例——这类题直接用“but for + 可预见结果”就能锁答案。

思维导图

先问：被告的酒驾，真的是这次死亡的原因吗？
第一步：酒后驾车 → 发生碰撞 → 死者死亡
第二步：看事实原因（actual cause）：but for 这次醉驾，碰撞会不会发生？
卡死点：题干说“即使没醉也会撞上”，所以事实原因断了。
第三步：就算酒驾违法，没了事实原因，manslaughter 也站不稳。
结论：最强抗辩是“碰撞本来就会发生”，对应选项 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他都喝到法定醉酒了，怎么还能脱罪？

但考试真正问的是：醉酒本身不是自动定罪点，真正要问的是这次死亡是不是由他的驾驶行为造成。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里换成刑法就是：不是“看起来很糟”就够了，得有因果关系。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的关键是：如果即使没喝酒也会发生碰撞，那就打断了事实原因（actual cause），被告最有希望脱罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 责任主观化

✕ A: 把醉酒当成自动免责，忽略了本题卡的是因果关系。

❌ 法律适用 | 罪名混搬

✕ B: 把no mens rea硬套到本题，但这里照样可能成立违法行为致死。

❌ 事实误判 | 共同原因错读

✕ D: 受害人有过错不等于被告没因果，题干没给你切断死亡链条。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看结果犯罪是否要求因果，再用“如果没有这行为，结果还会不会发生”秒杀选项。

考场速记

记住一句话：结果犯（result crime）先问but for，再问可预见；少了事实原因，后面的近因也白搭。

reason.en: The crime charged, requiring proof of causation and mens rea.
reason.zh: 指控的罪名，要求证明因果关系和主观意图。

reason.en: Indicates that the victim's death must be causally linked to the defendant's conduct.

reason.en: Incorrectly suggests voluntary intoxication negates mens rea for involuntary manslaughter.

reason.en: Confuses strict liability traffic violations with the requirements of misdemeanor manslaughter.

reason.zh: 为另一名驾驶员的行为是事故的唯一原因提供了事实支持。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant has been charged with battery for breaking a man's nose in a bar fight. At trial, the evidence established the following: The defendant was watching a contentious football game with the man when the defendant yelled obscenities about the man's favorite football team. In response to the defendant's remarks, the man yelled obscenities about the defendant. The defendant stood up from his chair, walked over to where the man was sitting, raised his fist and said, "One more word and I'll shut your mouth for you." The man then grabbed the defendant by the shirt and started waving a knife at the defendant in an effort to stab him. The defendant proceeded to punch the man several times until the man released the defendant's shirt.
Should the defendant be convicted of battery?

choices.A: No, because a person may use any amount of force to repel an attack.
choices.B: No, because the man attempted to use deadly force against him.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant failed to retreat.
choices.D: Yes, because the defendant was the initial aggressor.

questions.explanation:
Battery is the unlawful application of force (e.g., a punch) to another person that causes offensive contact or bodily harm (e.g., a black eye). Therefore, the defendant committed battery. However, an otherwise unlawful use of force may be justified if it was done in self-defense. This justification generally does not extend to an initial aggressor—i.e., the person who first uses or threatens physical force. However, an initial aggressor may gain the right to act in self-defense in two circumstances:

  • When the initial aggressor's use of nondeadly force is met with deadly force*
  • When the initial aggressor, in good faith, completely withdraws from the altercation and communicates that fact to the victim

Although merely using obscenities does not alone make a person an initial aggressor, the defendant assumed this role when he walked over to the man and threatened to strike him. The defendant's nondeadly threat was then met with deadly force when the man grabbed and waved a knife at the defendant in an attempt to stab him. This gave the defendant the right to act in self-defense by using reasonable force to prevent imminent unlawful harm to himself (Choices A & D).

Reasonable force means that a person may only use as much force as is required to repel the attack. Here, the defendant used reasonable force since he punched the man only until the man released the defendant's shirt. As a result, the battery against the man was justified and the defendant should not be convicted of this crime.

*The initial aggressor may not claim self-defense when he/she initially used deadly force against the victim.

(Choice C) There is no duty to retreat before using nondeadly force in self-defense (as seen here), even if there is an opportunity to do so safely.

📌 Educational Objective

An initial aggressor can only claim self-defense if (1) the aggressor's use of nondeadly force was met with deadly force or (2) the aggressor, in good faith, completely withdrew from the altercation and communicated that fact to the victim.

📚 References
  • 6 Am. Jur. 2d Assault and Battery § 53 (2020) (explaining when an initial aggressor gains the right to act in self-defense).
questions.zh-question:
一名被告因在酒吧斗殴中打断一名男子的鼻子而被指控犯有伤害罪(battery)。在庭审中，证据证实了以下事实：被告与该男子一同观看一场充满争议的橄榄球比赛时，被告对该男子最喜欢的球队大声辱骂。作为对被告言论的回应，该男子也对被告大声辱骂。被告从椅子上站起来，走到该男子坐的地方，举起拳头说：“你再说一个字，我就让你闭嘴。”该男子随后抓住被告的衬衫，并开始向被告挥舞刀具，试图刺伤他。被告于是连续击打该男子数拳，直到该男子松开被告的衬衫。

被告是否应被判犯有伤害罪(battery)？

zh-choices.A: 不应定罪，因为一个人可以使用任何程度的武力来抵御攻击。
zh-choices.B: 不应定罪，因为该男子试图对他使用致命武力。
zh-choices.C: 应该定罪，因为被告未能退让。
zh-choices.D: 应该定罪，因为被告是最初的攻击者。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Justification & excuse

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：先动手的人能不能靠自卫（self-defense）反打回去，关键看他先前是非致命攻击（nondeadly force）还是已经用了致命武力（deadly force）。

三秒认题路径：

先动手 → 对方升级 → 能否自卫 → 例外成立 → 选B

核心法律规则

battery（殴打）是对他人非法用力并造成有害或冒犯性接触。若行为人本来可构成 battery，但属于自卫（self-defense），就可能被正当化。

但初始侵害者（initial aggressor）通常不能先挑事再主张自卫；只有两种例外：对方把他的非致命武力（nondeadly force）升级成致命武力（deadly force），或他真诚撤退并明确告知对方。

本题里，走过去威胁出手的人先成了初始侵害者；对方随后持刀挥刺，已经把局面升级成致命武力，所以他可以用合理武力（reasonable force）挡回去。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题的控制规则是“初始侵害者遇到致命武力时可恢复自卫权”，所以答案转向正当化而不是定罪。

思维导图

先看：谁先把冲突升级成可归责的攻击？
题干事实先骂战队并不够；真正让他变成initial aggressor的是“走过去、举拳、说再说一句就打你”。
第二关对方是普通推搡，还是deadly force？
刀子挥刺 = 致命武力，触发初始侵害者的自卫例外
第三关他能不能只用到足以止住攻击的力？
能。只打到对方松开衣领为止，属于reasonable force。
结论自卫成立，battery 被正当化 → 不该定罪。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然他先站起来挑衅，那就一定是初始侵害者，不能再反打。

但考试真正问的是：对方后来有没有把冲突升级到致命武力（deadly force），让先动手的人重新拿回自卫权。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另外，failed to retreat 不是这题的陷阱：这里用的是非致命自卫，通常没有撤退义务。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的持刀挥刺把冲突升级成致命武力，先动手的人因此可以用合理武力自卫到对方松手为止。

❌ 概念混淆 | 绝对用力误判

✕ A: 把自卫当成可无限用力，错在忽略reasonable force。

❌ 法律适用 | 撤退义务误判

✕ C: 这里是非致命自卫场景，先不用找duty to retreat。

❌ 事实误判 | 先后顺序偷换

✕ D: 只看他先走过去不够，后面刀子一出，初始侵害者规则被例外打断。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判谁先升级冲突，再看对方有没有把局面推到致命武力。

考场速记

记住一句：初始侵害者（initial aggressor）只有在对方回以致命武力（deadly force），或自己真诚撤退并通知对方时，才可能重新主张自卫。

这题的速记就是：先挑事，不一定永远输；对方一上刀，你可能又能自卫。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A high school student's teacher told the student that she was going to receive a failing grade in history, which would prevent her from graduating. Furious, she reported to the principal that the teacher had fondled her, and he was fired. A year later, still unable to get work because of the scandal, the teacher committed suicide. The student, remorseful, confessed that her accusation had been false.
If the student is charged with manslaughter, what is her best defense?

choices.A: She acted under extreme emotional distress.
choices.B: She committed no act that proximately caused the teacher's death.
choices.C: She did not act with malice.
choices.D: She did not intend to cause the teacher's death.

questions.explanation:
Criminal causation
Actual (factual)
cause
  • Single cause – but for defendant's conduct, crime would not have occurred
  • Multiple causes – defendant's conduct was substantial factor causing crime
Proximate (legal)
cause
  • Crime was natural, probable & foreseeable consequence of defendant's conduct

There are two types of manslaughter:

  • Voluntary – an intentional killing mitigated by adequate provocation (ie, heat-of-passion killing) or, in some jurisdictions, other mitigating factors (eg, imperfect self-defense)
  • Involuntary – an unintentional killing committed with criminal negligence or during an unlawful act (eg, misdemeanor manslaughter)

A conviction of either crime requires proof that the defendant's conduct was both the actual ("but for") cause and proximate (foreseeable) cause of the victim's death.

Here, the teacher committed suicide after the student falsely accused him of fondling her. The student would likely be charged with involuntary manslaughter since there is no evidence that she intended to cause the teacher's death (Choice D). And though the teacher would not have died but for the student's accusation (actual causation), the student is not guilty of manslaughter if she committed no act that proximately caused that death—ie, if the suicide was unforeseeable. Therefore, that is the student's best defense.

(Choice A) Extreme emotional distress is not a defense to a crime—but it can be a mitigating factor at sentencing. Here, however, the student's distress at her failing grade would hardly mitigate a false sexual-misconduct report.

(Choice C) Malice aforethought is a requirement for murder—not manslaughter.

📌 Educational Objective

A manslaughter conviction requires proof that the defendant's conduct was both the actual ("but for") and proximate (foreseeable) cause of the victim's death.
questions.zh-question:
一名高中生的历史老师告诉该学生，她的历史课成绩将不及格，这将导致她无法毕业。学生一怒之下向校长举报说老师抚摸了她，老师因此被解雇。一年后，这位老师因为这桩丑闻仍然找不到工作，于是自杀身亡。学生心生悔意，承认她的指控是虚假的。

如果该学生被控过失杀人罪 (manslaughter)，她最好的辩护理由是什么？

zh-choices.A: 她的行为是在极端情绪困扰下作出的。
zh-choices.B: 她的行为并未近因导致老师的死亡。
zh-choices.C: 她的行为不带恶意 (malice)。
zh-choices.D: 她无意导致老师的死亡。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：过失致死（manslaughter）是否需要证明被告行为同时构成实际因果和近因因果，尤其是自杀结果是否可预见。

三秒认题路径：

自杀结果 → 因果关系 → 可预见性 → 不能立上诉 → 选 B

核心法律规则

过失致死（manslaughter）要成立，检方必须证明被告行为既是事实原因（actual cause，考场意思：没有这一下就不会死），也是近因原因（proximate cause，考场意思：死亡必须是自然、可能、可预见的后果）。

这里即使学生的诬告让老师丢工作，真正卡分点还是：老师后来自杀这一步，是否对学生来说是可预见的死亡链条。

因为题干没有显示学生想杀人，也没有显示她能预见老师会自杀，所以她最强的抗辩就是：她的行为没有法律上的近因。

核心判例： 无。本题直接按因果关系规则判断：可预见性（foreseeability）不到，就卡死过失致死。

思维导图

先问：老师的死亡能不能算学生的过失致死结果？
第一关有无 实际因果（actual cause）？
有：若不是学生诬告，老师不会失去工作，也不会走到自杀这一步。
第二关有无 近因因果（proximate cause）？
要看死亡是不是自然、可能、可预见的后果。
卡死点：老师自杀若属不可预见，就断在近因，不能定 manslaughter。
结论即使有事实原因，没有可预见的死亡链条，学生就有最好抗辩。
答案走向：选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：老师确实因为她的假指控丢了工作，感觉很“惨”，所以她应该负责到底。

但考试真正问的是：她能不能为死亡负责，不是为“名誉受损”或“工作丢了”负责。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键点是老师后来自杀，而学生未必能预见这一死亡链条；没有近因因果，就不能成立 manslaughter。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 extreme emotional 当成免罪理由了。

❌ 法律适用 | 罪名要件错位

✕ C: 你把 malice 搬来，但那是 murder 的门槛。

❌ 事实误判 | 夸大意图要求

✕ D: 题目问的是过失致死，不要求她真想让老师死。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看死亡链条，再拆实际因果和近因因果，别被“她很坏”带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：manslaughter 也要看 actual cause + proximate cause，只要死亡结果对被告来说不够可预见，近因就断掉。

做题口诀：先问“有没有这一下”，再问“死得够不够可预见”；只要后者断了，答案通常就往被告这边走。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question: In which of the following situations would a court applying common law doctrine be most likely to convict a defendant of the crime charged, despite the defendant's mistake?

choices.A: The defendant was charged with assault with intent to rape a woman who he mistakenly believed had agreed to have sexual intercourse with him.
choices.B: The defendant was charged with bigamy. He married his neighbor four years after her husband was reported missing at sea. The rescued husband returns alive. A state statute provides that a person is presumed dead after five years of unexplained absence. The defendant believed the statutory period was three years.
choices.C: The defendant was charged with burglary. He had broken into an office where he once worked and had taken a typewriter that he erroneously believed had been given to him before he was fired.
choices.D: The defendant was charged with murder after he shot and killed a man who had extorted money from him. The defendant mistakenly thought the victim had raised his hand to shoot when, in fact, the victim was shaking his fist at the defendant to frighten him.

questions.explanation:
Mistake of law v. Mistake of fact
Definition Applicability
Mistake of law Defendant mistakenly believes conduct not prohibited by law
  • No defense unless:
    • Law prohibiting conduct was unavailable
    • Defendant reasonably relied on invalid law
    • Mistake negates mens rea*
Mistake of
fact		 Defendant is mistaken as to a matter of fact
  • When mistake negates mens rea:
    • Specific intent – defense if honest mistake
    • General intent & malice – defense if honest & reasonable mistake
    • Strict liability – no defense
*Mens rea – state of mind necessary to be guilty of criminal offense.

Mistake of fact is a defense to criminal liability for:

  • specific intent crimes – when the defendant's honest mistake, even if unreasonable, negates the requisite mens rea and
  • general intent crimes – when the defendant's honest and reasonable mistake negates the requisite mens rea.

But mistake of law is almost never a defense to criminal liability. As a result, the court would likely convict the defendant of bigamy—ie, marrying someone who already has a living spouse—despite his mistaken belief that the neighbor's husband was presumed by law to be dead.

(Choice A) Assault with intent to rape requires proof that the defendant specifically intended to commit rape—at common law, sexual intercourse with a woman (other than the defendant's wife) against her will by force or threat of force. Since the defendant's mistaken belief that the woman had agreed to sexual intercourse shows that he did not intend to rape her, he would not be convicted of assault with intent to rape.

(Choice C) Common law burglary is the breaking and entering of another's dwelling at night with the specific intent to commit a felony therein. Here, the defendant's mistaken belief that the typewriter was his negates the necessary intent to commit a felony (no intent to steal). Therefore, he would not be convicted of burglary.

(Choice D) Common law murder is an unlawful killing committed with malice aforethought. But murder may be reduced to voluntary manslaughter when, as here, the defendant mistakenly believed that deadly force was necessary for self-defense. So the defendant would likely be convicted of voluntary manslaughter—not murder.

📌 Educational Objective

An honest mistake of fact is a defense to specific intent crimes (even if unreasonable) and general intent crimes (if reasonable) when it negates the requisite mens rea. But mistake of law is almost never a defense.
questions.zh-question: 在下列哪种情况下，适用普通法原则的法院最有可能在被告人存在认识错误的情况下，仍判定其所控罪名成立？

zh-choices.A: 被告人被控意图强奸的攻击罪，他错误地认为该女性已同意与他发生性关系。
zh-choices.B: 被告人被控重婚罪。他在其邻居的丈夫据报在海上失踪四年后与她结婚。之后，被救回的丈夫活着回来了。一项州法律规定，无故失踪五年后，该人即被推定死亡。被告人认为该法定期限是三年。
zh-choices.C: 被告人被控入室犯法罪。他闯入了他曾经工作过的一间办公室，并拿走了一台他错误地认为在被解雇前已赠予他的打字机。
zh-choices.D: 被告人因开枪打死一名曾向他勒索金钱的男子而被控谋杀罪。被告人错误地认为受害人举手准备开枪，而事实上，受害人只是在向被告人挥舞拳头以吓唬他。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Mens Rea- State of Mind

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：错误认知（mistake）到底是事实错误（mistake of fact）还是法律错误（mistake of law），以及它能不能打掉 mens rea（犯意）。

三秒认题路径：

先看错什么 → 再分法/事实 → 事实错可抗辩 → 法律错几乎不行 → 选能定罪的

核心法律规则

事实错误（mistake of fact）是对“客观事实”认错；如果它把 mens rea（犯意）打没了，就可能抗辩成功。对特定故意犯罪（specific intent crime），只要是诚实错误，哪怕不合理，也可能成立抗辩；对普通故意/恶意犯罪（general intent / malice），通常要诚实且合理的错误才行。

法律错误（mistake of law）是把“法律允许不允许”看错了；它几乎从来不是抗辩，除非法律本身不可得、被错误但合理地依赖了无效法律，或错误刚好让 mens rea（犯意） 消失。

核心判例： 没有特别判例点名时，本题直接套“法律错误几乎不抗辩；事实错误看是否打掉犯意”。

思维导图

先问：错的是“事实”还是“法律”？
事实错看它有没有打掉 mens rea（犯意）
若是 specific intent（特定故意） → 诚实错误就可能救你
若是 general intent / malice（普通故意 / 恶意） → 通常要诚实且合理
若是 strict liability（严格责任） → 错误直接卡死：不能抗辩
再问：错的是不是“法律允许不允许”
法律错原则上不抗辩
只有三种少数例外：法律不可得、合理依赖无效法、错误反而否掉犯意
本题 bigamy 属法律错误路线，通常不能靠“我以为法律是三年”脱身
结论：选会被定罪的那一项，不是最“可怜”的那一项。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告“真心以为”自己没犯法，所以应该无罪。

但考试真正问的是：你错的是事实还是法律。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里 bigamy（重婚） 的关键不是他有没有误会丈夫是否死亡，而是他误会的是法律推定死亡的期限，这就是典型mistake of law（法律错误）。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的 five years 法定推定死亡期限被他看成三年，错的是法律规则，不是事实，所以法院最可能仍然定罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 specific intent 题硬套进来，实际上这里在问法律错误能不能挡罪。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ C: 以为偷走打字机就成了“合理误拿”，但题干是在借 burglary 误导你看错犯罪类型。

❌ 法律适用 | 正当防卫误套

✕ D: 把 self-defense 的误信当成可以直接无罪，但这题主轴是法律错误，不是杀人抗辩细分。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“错的是事实还是法律”，再看该错误能不能真正打掉犯意。

考场速记

记住一句话：事实错误先看能否打掉 mens rea（犯意）；法律错误几乎不救人。遇到“我以为法律是这样”的题，先往法律错误走，别被诚意感带跑。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
The chief executive officer (CEO) of a company that operated a knitting mill delegated all operational decision-making to the supervisor of the mill. The child labor laws in the jurisdiction provide, "It is a violation of the law for one to employ a person under the age of 17 years for full-time labor."
Without the CEO's knowledge, the supervisor hired a number of 15- and 16-year-olds to work at the mill full time. He did not ask their ages and they did not disclose them. The supervisor could have discovered their ages easily by asking for identification, but he did not do so because he was not aware of the law and believed that company policy was to hire young people.
If the statute is interpreted to create strict liability and the supervisor is charged with violating it, what is the proper verdict?

choices.A: Guilty, because he hired the children.
choices.B: Guilty, because he should have inquired as to the ages of the children.
choices.C: Not guilty, because he believed he was following company policy and was not aware of the violation.
choices.D: Not guilty, because the knitting mill, not the supervisor, is the employer of the children.

questions.explanation:
A person is guilty of any crime that he/she personally committed—even if that crime was committed on another's behalf or within the scope of employment. And guilt for a strict liability crime (as seen here) arises once a person commits the unlawful act—regardless of the person's fault or mens rea.

Here, the supervisor—who had all operational decision-making authority for the knitting mill—hired 15- and 16-year-olds for full-time labor at the mill. And though the mill is the children's employer, the supervisor personally violated the child labor statute when he hired them. Therefore, he is guilty of this strict liability crime (Choice D).

(Choice B) Though inquiring into the children's ages before hiring them would have been prudent, failing to do so is not a violation of the statute or a basis for the supervisor's guilt.

(Choice C) Evidence that the supervisor believed he was following company policy (mistake of fact) and was not aware of the violation (mistake of law) goes to the supervisor's mens rea. But since a defendant's mens rea is irrelevant to strict liability crimes, these mistakes are no defense.

📌 Educational Objective

A person is liable for any crime that he/she commits personally—even while acting on another's behalf or within the scope of employment.

一家经营针织厂的公司的首席执行官 (CEO) 将所有经营决策权授予了工厂主管。

该司法管辖区的童工法规定：“雇佣未满17岁者从事全职工作属于违法行为。”

在CEO不知情的情况下，主管雇佣了数名15岁和16岁的青少年在工厂全职工作。他没有询问他们的年龄，他们也没有透露。主管本可以通过要求出示身份证明轻易地发现他们的年龄，但他没有这样做，因为他不知道有这项法律，并认为公司政策就是雇佣年轻人。

如果该法规被解释为创设严格责任（strict liability），且主管被指控违反该法规，那么正确的裁决是什么？

zh-choices.A: 有罪，因为他雇佣了这些孩子。
zh-choices.B: 有罪，因为他本应询问这些孩子的年龄。
zh-choices.C: 无罪，因为他认为自己是在遵守公司政策，并且不知道自己的行为违法。
zh-choices.D: 无罪，因为针织厂才是这些孩子的雇主，而不是主管。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Mens Rea- State of Mind

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：严格责任（strict liability）下，行为人自己亲手实施违法行为时，就会被定罪，不因“我以为公司政策允许”而免责。

三秒认题路径：

严格责任 → 自己亲做 → 无需故意 → 误信政策无用 → 选有罪

核心法律规则

严格责任（strict liability）的考场意思：只要你亲自实施（personally committed）了法条禁止的动作，mens rea（主观罪过）就不是这道题的门槛。

这里问的不是“谁是雇主”，而是“谁亲手雇了未满17岁的人做全职工作”。所以即使他是在公司权限内办事，仍然是他自己违反了童工法。

核心判例：N/A。本题直接用严格责任规则：行为人亲手做了禁行为，就定罪。

思维导图

先看是不是严格责任：是。
问题1他有没有亲自做违法动作？
有：他亲自雇用15、16岁孩子全职上班。
问题2还能拿 mens rea 抗辩吗？
不能：严格责任不看“我不知道法”。
结论公司是雇主，不影响他个人因亲手违法而有罪。
答案：有罪，选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：“不是公司雇的，所以主管不该背罪”。

但考试真正问的是：谁亲手实施了禁行为，不是谁在合同上被写成雇主。

这里看的是“亲自做了没有”，不是“职位上是不是老板”。

另一个坑是把 mistake of fact（事实错误）、mistake of law（法律错误） 当成救命绳；对严格责任来说，这两种都不救人。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干关键事实是他亲自招聘了未满17岁的孩子做全职工作；亲手实施了法条禁止的行为，严格责任下直接有罪。

❌ 事实误判 | 过度勤勉误判

✕ B: 把“最好先查年龄”偷换成法定义务。

❌ 法律适用 | 误把抗辩搬来

✕ C: 以为 company policy 能洗掉严格责任。

❌ 概念混淆 | 雇主身份混淆

✕ D: 抓住“公司是雇主”就放过主管，错把组织身份当成个人免责。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定行为人是否亲自做了禁行为，再看题目是否明确写了严格责任；写了就别找 mens rea。

考场速记

记住一句：严格责任看行为，不看心里话。谁亲手做了法条禁止的动作，谁就先站到有罪这一边。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A fan and his friend were watching a football game at the fan's home when they began to argue. The friend became abusive, and the fan asked him to leave. The friend refused, walked into the kitchen, picked up a knife, and said he would cut the fan's heart out. The fan pulled a gun from under the sofa, walked to his front door, opened it, and again told the friend to leave. The friend again refused. Instead, he walked slowly toward the fan, brandishing the knife in a threatening manner. The fan, rather than running out the door himself, shot in the friend's direction, intending only to scare him. However, the bullet struck the friend, killing him instantly.
The fan is charged with murder.
Should he be convicted?

choices.A: No, because he did not intend to kill his friend.
choices.B: No, because he was acting in self-defense and had no duty to retreat.
choices.C: Yes, because he had a clear opportunity and duty to retreat.
choices.D: Yes, because the use of deadly force was unreasonable under the circumstances.

questions.explanation:
Self-defense
(justification for criminal conduct)
General requirements Duty to retreat
Nondeadly force
  • Actual & reasonable belief of imminent unlawful harm
  • Force reasonably necessary to prevent harm
  • Not initial aggressor
  • No duty to retreat
Deadly force
  • Actual & reasonable belief of imminent serious harm or death
  • Deadly force necessary to prevent harm
  • Not initial aggressor
  • Majority rule: No duty to retreat
  • Minority rule: Duty when safe retreat available unless inside one's home

Murder requires proof that a person unlawfully killed another with malice aforethought. But the use of deadly force in self-defense justifies a killing and serves as a defense to murder if the person:

  • actually and reasonably believed that such force was necessary to prevent imminent serious bodily harm or death and
  • was not the initial aggressor—ie, did not engage in physical force first or intentionally provoke the altercation.

Under the majority rule, there is no duty to retreat before using deadly force in self-defense. And though a minority of jurisdictions require retreat before using deadly force if it is safe to do so, a person never has a duty to retreat in his/her own home.

Here, the fan shot and killed his friend. But the fan actually and reasonably believed that he needed to use deadly force in self-defense because (1) the friend had threatened to cut out the fan's heart and (2) was walking toward him while brandishing a knife. Additionally, the fan was not the initial aggressor, so he justifiably shot his friend in self-defense (Choice D). And though the fan had a clear opportunity to run out the open front door, he had no duty to retreat since he was in his own home (Choice C). Therefore, the fan should not be convicted of murder.

(Choice A) A person may be convicted of murder—even if there was no intent to kill—if the person recklessly disregarded a high risk of serious bodily harm or death (ie, depraved-heart murder). Since the fan recklessly disregarded the high risk that the fired bullet would hit and kill the friend, the fan's lack of intent to kill will not prevent his conviction.

📌 Educational Objective

Deadly force can be used in self-defense when a person (1) actually and reasonably believes that such force is necessary to prevent imminent serious harm or death and (2) is not the initial aggressor. There is generally no duty to retreat before using such force—especially when a person is inside his/her home.
questions.zh-question:
一名球迷和他的朋友在该球迷家中观看一场橄榄球比赛时开始争吵。朋友开始辱骂，球迷要求他离开。朋友拒绝了，并走进厨房，拿起一把刀，说要挖出球迷的心脏。球迷从沙发下拔出一把枪，走到前门，打开门，再次要求朋友离开。朋友再次拒绝。相反，他以威胁的方式挥舞着刀，缓缓走向球迷。球迷没有自己跑出门，而是朝朋友的方向开了一枪，意图只是吓唬他。然而，子弹击中了朋友，致其当场死亡。

该球迷被控谋杀罪。

他是否应被定罪？

zh-choices.A: 不应定罪，因为他无意杀死他的朋友。
zh-choices.B: 不应定罪，因为他是在进行正当防卫，并且没有退让义务。
zh-choices.C: 应该定罪，因为他有明确的退让机会和退让义务。
zh-choices.D: 应该定罪，因为在这种情况下使用致命武力是不合理的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Specific defenses

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：在自己家里，面对持刀威胁时，是否可以以自卫（self-defense）作为杀人罪的抗辩，以及是否存在退避义务（duty to retreat）。

三秒认题路径：

家中冲突 → 持刀逼近 → 合理恐惧 → 先看自卫 → 无退避义务

核心法律规则

自卫（self-defense）的考试判断很简单：先看被告是否实际且合理地相信（actually and reasonably believed）自己正面临迫在眉睫的严重伤害或死亡（imminent serious bodily harm or death），再看他用的是否是必要的致命武力。非初始挑衅者（not the initial aggressor）才能走这条抗辩路。

对致命武力（deadly force），多数法域通常没有退避义务（no duty to retreat）；而且人在自己家里，考试上几乎一定先想到“可以站住不跑”。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用于本题；本题锁定的是普通法自卫规则：在家中面对致命威胁，通常不要求先退避。

思维导图

先问：这是致命武力自卫吗？
事实触发：对方拿刀、说要“割心”，还一步步逼近。
规则门槛：被告必须实际且合理地相信有imminent 重大伤害或死亡。
再问：他是不是先动手的那个人？
这题答案：不是。友人先持刀威胁，风扇不是初始挑衅者。
最后问：他有没有必须先跑？
家中规则：在自己家里，通常没有退避义务。
结论：不能因为“他明明有门可跑”就否定自卫。
所以：自卫成立 → 谋杀罪抗辩成立 → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他都已经把门打开了，明明有机会跑，为什么还能自卫？

但考试真正问的是：司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。本题对应到自卫就是：看法律上有没有退避义务，不是看你有没有“更安全的逃跑选择”。

另一层陷阱是“我只想吓人，不想杀人”，这在这里救不了他，因为谋杀可以由鲁莽漠视严重风险成立；真正能挡住指控的是自卫，而不是主观没想杀。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干持刀逼近并扬言割心，足以支持他对致命危险的合理相信；又因他在自己家中，通常没有退避义务（no duty to retreat），所以可成立自卫。

❌ 概念混淆 | 误把故意当必要

✕ A: 只盯着did not intend，忽略谋杀也可能由鲁莽杀伤成立。

❌ 事实误判 | 夸大可逃事实

✕ C: 把clear opportunity 直接等同必须退避，但在家中通常没有这个义务。

❌ 法律适用 | 把武力标准抬错

✕ D: 只因他先开枪就说unreasonable，却没算上持刀逼近的即时威胁。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先抓是否存在致命威胁和家中场景，再判断有没有退避义务。

考场速记

记住一句话：家中遇致命威胁，先看自卫，不先逼他跑。遇到退避义务题，先把“我有没有在自己家里”放到脑子最前面。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是上诉例外记忆法；但本题不是上诉题，真正要背的是“在家里对致命威胁，通常不用先退避”。

reason.en: Places the encounter inside the actor's home, which matters for retreat rules.
reason.zh: 表明冲突发生在被告家中，影响是否负有退避义务。

reason.en: Shows the friend escalated by moving to a more dangerous area and arming himself.
reason.zh: 说明朋友进一步升级冲突并取刀。

reason.en: Creates the apparent deadly threat needed for self-defense analysis.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
An off-duty doctor was jogging one evening when he came upon an elderly woman who had suffered a severe heart attack while walking her dogs. The woman was not breathing, and the doctor could barely detect a pulse. The doctor immediately began CPR on the woman while a bystander called 911. The doctor was able to resuscitate the woman but, in the process of performing CPR, broke several of her ribs. The broken ribs punctured the woman's lungs, causing them to collapse and leaving her unable to breathe. Because the doctor did not have the necessary medical instruments to release the air that was trapped inside of the woman's lungs, the doctor did nothing further to help her. The woman subsequently died from suffocation before an ambulance arrived.
Is the doctor criminally liable for the woman's death?

choices.A: No, because it was not reasonably possible for the doctor to help the woman.
choices.B: No, because the doctor was not under a legal duty to help the woman.
choices.C: Yes, because the doctor, as a medical professional, was under a legal duty to help the woman.
choices.D: Yes, because the doctor stopped rendering aid to the woman after breaking her ribs.

questions.explanation:
Legal duty to act
(subject to criminal liability if breach)
Special relationship Parent/child, spouses, employer/employee
Assumption of care Once person renders aid, liable for making victim's condition worse
(ie, detrimental undertaking)
Created risk of harm Person who falsely imprisons another & fails to provide food is liable for resulting death
Statute imposes duty "Off-duty nurses must render aid to injured persons"
Contract imposes duty "Employer will administer first aid in case of emergency"
Mnemonic:  Specific Acts Can Spawn Crimes

Criminal liability can arise from a failure to act (ie, an omission) if the defendant:

  • had a legal duty to act and
  • could have reasonably done so.

A legal duty to act is imposed when a person voluntarily assumes care of another—eg, by rendering aid in a medical emergency. As a result, a voluntary rescuer has a duty to take all reasonable steps to provide care to the rescuee and may be criminally liable for omissions during the process. But such omissions will not result in criminal liability if the omitted action could not reasonably be performed.

Here, by rendering aid after finding the woman unconscious, the doctor voluntarily assumed a legal duty to take all reasonable steps to help her (Choice B). However, he subsequently failed to relieve the pressure in the woman's lungs caused by his administration of necessary CPR. But since the doctor lacked the medical equipment necessary to do so, it was not reasonably possible for him to perform the omitted act. Therefore, he is not criminally liable for the woman's death (Choice D).

(Choice C) The doctor was not under a legal duty to help the woman simply because he was a medical professional. Instead, his duty to act on the woman's behalf was imposed when he voluntarily assumed care of the woman by rendering aid.

📌 Educational Objective

Criminal liability can arise from a failure to act if the defendant had a legal duty to act (eg, by voluntarily assuming care of another) and could have reasonably done so. However, omissions in performing that duty will not result in criminal liability if the omitted action could not reasonably be performed.

该医生对该妇女的死亡是否负有刑事责任？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为医生在合理情况下不可能帮助该妇女。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为医生没有法律义务去帮助该妇女。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该医生作为一名医疗专业人员，有法律义务帮助该妇女。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为医生在压断该妇女的肋骨后停止了提供救助。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Actus Reus- Acts and Omissions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：故意不作为（omission）是否会触发刑责，关键看被告是否已经因救助而承担了 法律上的救助义务（legal duty to act），以及他后续的动作是否 reasonably possible。

三秒认题路径：

先救人 → 先有义务 → 还做得到吗 → 做不到就不罚 → 选 A

核心法律规则

刑法里的 不作为（omission），一般只有在被告先有 法律义务（legal duty） 却又能合理做到而没做时，才可能成立犯罪。这里最重要的触发点不是“他是不是医生”，而是他是否已经通过 主动救助（voluntary assumption of care） 接过了救助责任。

一旦他开始帮忙，就不能只做一半然后放任风险扩大；但如果最后那一步根本没有必要器材，客观上做不到，就不会因为没做那一步而被定罪。考试上你要抓的是：duty 有了以后，还得看 reasonably possible 过不过关。

核心判例： 本题的控制逻辑就是 主动承担照护义务（voluntary assumption of care），但未完成的补救动作若客观上做不到，通常不成立刑责。

思维导图

先看：这是单纯“不救”，还是“救到一半后停手”?
是救到一半：医生先做了 CPR，说明他已经 主动承担照护（voluntary assumption of care）。
再问：后面没做的那步，客观上能不能做？
不能做：没有必要医疗器材，无法释放肺内积气，第三要件卡死。
结论：有义务，但未完成动作 not reasonably possible → 不成立刑责 → 选 A。
别被带偏：“他是医生”不是自动义务来源；真正义务来自他已经开始救人。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然病人最后死了，而且医生已经把人救活一点又停手，那当然要负责。

但考试真正问的是：法律程序上能不能救济这一步有没有可行性，不是看结果多惨；司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题最会骗人的地方，是把“医生身份”当成固定救助义务；其实题目已经给了更精确的义务来源：他自己先出手了。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干关键在于医生后续要做的补救动作 没有必要医疗器材，所以那一步客观上做不到；有义务不等于必须对不可能完成的动作负责。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ B: 把 medical professional 当成自动义务来源，题目不认。

❌ 法律适用 | 身份义务误套

✕ C: 只盯着“他是医生”，忽略义务其实来自他先救人。

❌ 事实误判 | 结果归责偷换

✕ D: 把 stopped rendering aid 当成足够定罪，漏看他根本做不到下一步。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“是否已经承担照护义务”，再立刻检查被遗漏的动作能不能现实完成。

考场速记

记忆口诀：Specific Acts Can Spawn Crimes。先有明确义务，再看你有没有能力完成；有义务但做不到，通常不罚。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man who believed that his wife was cheating on him with her gym trainer decided to kill the trainer. He loaded his handgun and set off for the trainer's house. Because he was anxious about committing the crime, the man first stopped at a bar, drank eight shots of hard liquor, and became intoxicated. He then left the bar and went to the trainer's house. When the trainer answered the door, the man shot and killed him. The man then passed out on the trainer's porch.
The man has been charged with murder in a jurisdiction that follows the common law.
Can the man raise an intoxication defense?

choices.A: No, because drinking at the bar was the proximate cause of the killing.
choices.B: No, because the man intended to commit the murder and drank to strengthen his nerve.
choices.C: Yes, because drinking at the bar was a foreseeable intervening cause of the killing.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's intoxication negated the specific intent required for murder.

questions.explanation:
Intoxication defense

Type of crime Definition Voluntary Involuntary
Specific intent Act consciously performed for particular purpose ✓ ✓
General intent Act consciously performed ✓
Strict liability Act performed ✓

A defendant may be able to raise an intoxication defense if he/she was intoxicated when the crime was committed due to either:

  • Involuntary intoxication – the unknowing or forcible ingestion of an intoxicating substance is a defense if it placed the defendant in the same mental state required for an insanity defense.
  • Voluntary intoxication – the deliberate ingestion of a substance that the defendant knew or should have known has intoxicating effects is only a defense to specific intent crimes if the intoxication prevented the defendant from forming such intent.

At common law, murder is defined as the unlawful killing of another with malice aforethought. Although voluntary intoxication is no defense if the defendant acted with reckless malice aforethought, it may negate a defendant's specific intent to kill. But such intent is not negated if the defendant became intoxicated to commit the crime.

Here, the man decided to kill the trainer because he thought that the trainer and his wife were having an affair (specific intent to kill). He had deliberately ingested eight shots of hard liquor at a bar before he went to the trainer's house (voluntary intoxication) and therefore was intoxicated when he killed the trainer. But since the man had become intoxicated to strengthen his nerve to commit the murder, intoxication is no defense (Choice D).

(Choice A) Proximate causation exists when it was foreseeable that the defendant's conduct would kill the victim. Although common law murder requires proof that the defendant proximately caused the victim's death, it has no bearing on whether intoxication is a valid defense.

(Choice C) An unforeseeable intervening cause—an event that happens after the defendant acts but before harm occurs—may eliminate the proximate causation required for a crime. But a foreseeable intervening cause will not. And even if an unforeseeable intervening cause had occurred (eg, had a plane crashed into the trainer's home), it would not impact the man's ability to raise an intoxication defense. Instead, it would serve as a separate defense.

📌 Educational Objective

Involuntary intoxication is a defense if it placed the defendant in the same mental state required for an insanity defense. Voluntary intoxication is a defense to specific intent crimes if the intoxication kept the defendant from forming such intent. But it is not a defense if the defendant became intoxicated to commit the crime.

在一个遵循普通法的司法管辖区，该男子被指控犯有谋杀罪。

该男子能否提出醉酒抗辩？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为在酒吧喝酒是这起杀人案的近因。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为该男子意图实施谋杀，并且喝酒是为了壮胆。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为在酒吧喝酒是这起杀人案中一个可预见的介入原因。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该男子的醉酒状态排除了谋杀罪所要求的特定意图。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Responsibility

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：自愿醉酒（voluntary intoxication）能不能替被告挡掉故意杀人（murder）所需的特定故意。

三秒认题路径：

先自愿饮酒 → 再去杀人 → 看特定故意 → 不是抗辩

核心法律规则

自愿醉酒（voluntary intoxication），就是自己故意喝进去，考场意思：只在特定故意（specific intent）犯罪里才可能帮忙，前提是它真的让你形成不了那个故意。

非自愿醉酒（involuntary intoxication），就是被迫或不知情地摄入，考场意思：它像精神障碍抗辩一样去看，但本题不是这个路子。

这里是普通法谋杀（murder），关键看被告有没有想杀人的特定意图；如果他是为了“壮胆”才喝酒，考试就直接判：不能拿醉酒当盾牌。

核心判例： 无须特定判例 — 本题直接套用普通法醉酒规则：为了犯罪而喝醉，不让你用醉酒否定故意。

思维导图

先问：这是终局判决吗？
YES可以正常上诉，不用扯醉酒抗辩。
NO继续看被告是否真的靠醉酒挡掉了故意。
这题的法律关卡：自愿喝酒 + 特定故意谋杀
先看事实：先决定杀人，再去酒吧喝了八杯，最后去开枪。
卡死点：他喝酒是为了strengthen his nerve，不是喝到失去形成故意的能力。
结论
自愿醉酒不能救他，答案落在 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他喝了八杯，既然醉了，就应该能把谋杀里的故意冲掉。

但考试真正问的是：他醉酒是不是为了让自己更敢杀人；如果是，这种醉酒不会替他洗掉特定故意。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的失控有没有发生」。这里不是比谁醉得更重，而是看醉酒有没有真正阻止形成杀人意图。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的先有杀人决定、后去喝酒壮胆，说明他不是被醉酒挡住了故意，而是靠酒精给自己壮胆后仍去杀人。

❌ 事实误判 | 代理因果偷换

✕ A: 把 proximate cause 搬来乱套，醉酒不是杀人的近因抗辩。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间原因误套

✕ C: 把 intervening cause 当成醉酒抗辩，方向完全错了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 特定故意误读

✕ D: 只看 specific intent 就想放行，但他是为杀人而喝醉，故意没被醉酒否掉。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“自愿还是非自愿”，再看“喝酒是挡故意还是壮胆杀人”，最后直接对答案。

考场速记

记住一句：自愿醉酒只可能帮你挡特定故意（specific intent），但如果你是为了犯罪去喝醉，答案通常还是“不能抗辩”。

这题的速记就是：drink to strengthen nerve，不是给你脱罪，是给你定罪。

  • other mitigating factors (eg, imperfect self-defense)
Involuntary
manslaughter		 Unintentional killing either:
  • caused by criminal negligence (or recklessness under MPC)
  • occurs during commission of criminal act (eg, misdemeanor manslaughter)

MPC = Model Penal Code.

Murder is an unlawful killing committed with malice aforethought. The malice-aforethought requirement can be satisfied by any of these mental states:

  • intent to kill
  • intent to inflict serious bodily injury
  • reckless disregard of an obvious or unjustifiably high risk of causing death or serious bodily injury (ie, depraved-heart murder) or
  • intent to commit an inherently dangerous felony (ie, felony-murder rule).

Here, the defendant intended to inflict a serious injury when he struck the victim in the face with a baseball bat. And since the victim died as a result, the defendant is guilty of murder—even though he did not intend to kill the victim. Therefore, this defendant is most likely to be convicted of the charged offense.

(Choice A) Arson is the malicious (ie, intentional or reckless) burning of any structure. But this defendant did not intend to burn the store. Nor did he recklessly disregard an obvious or high risk that disabling the store's burglary alarm would result in a fire. Therefore, he is unlikely to be convicted of arson.

(Choice C) Involuntary manslaughter is an unintentional killing committed with criminal negligence or during an unlawful act. But this defendant is unlikely to be convicted of this crime since he did not grossly deviate from a reasonable standard of care, or commit an unlawful act, by pranking the victim with a plastic rattlesnake.

(Choice D) Attempt always requires proof of specific intent to commit the target crime. And since there is no indication that this defendant intended to introduce adulterated aspirin into interstate commerce, he is unlikely to be convicted of attempt. This is true even though the completed crime is likely a strict liability offense.

📌 Educational Objective

Murder need not be committed with the intent to kill. Instead, this crime can be committed with any type of malice aforethought—eg, intent to inflict serious bodily injury.

zh-choices.A: 被告对一家珠宝店实施了入室犯法罪 (burglary)，意图盗窃一些钻石。在他进入商店时，他使商店的防盗警报系统短路，从而阻止了警方接到他进入的警报。闷燃的电线最终引发火灾，烧毁了商店。被告被控犯有纵火罪。
zh-choices.B: 被告用棒球棒击打受害人面部，意图造成严重伤害。受害人住院三天后死亡。被告被控犯有谋杀罪。
zh-choices.C: 被告想通过将一条塑料响尾蛇放入受害人朋友的午餐盒中来吓唬他。当受害人误拿了那个午餐盒并打开，以为是自己的时，塑料响尾蛇弹了出来。由于受到惊吓，受害人心脏病发作死亡。被告被控犯有非自愿过失杀人罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：谋杀（murder）不一定要“想杀人”，只要有恶意预谋（malice aforethought）里的“想造成严重伤害”也能定谋杀。

三秒认题路径：

想打伤人 → 人死了 → 先看恶意预谋 → 伤害故意也够 → 选谋杀

核心法律规则

谋杀（murder）的门槛是恶意预谋（malice aforethought），考场上不只等于“想杀”。

只要行为人有意图造成严重身体伤害（intent to inflict serious bodily injury），而死亡真的发生，就可以进谋杀。

这里的关键不是他有没有“想让人死”，而是他是不是已经带着足够坏的主观心态出手了。

核心判例：本题不用背具体案名，直接抓规则：恶意预谋（malice aforethought）包含“想造成严重伤害”，所以伤人致死可定谋杀。

思维导图

先问：他有没有 恶意预谋（malice aforethought）？
YES意图造成严重伤害 → 打中脸部的棒球棍 → 伤势足够重
再看：人有没有死？
YES三天后死亡 → 结论：谋杀成立，不能说“我没想杀”就逃掉
NO若只有轻微冲突、无严重伤害故意 → 才要往更轻罪名看
这题的考场逻辑：想造成重伤 + 真的死了 = 直接推到 谋杀（murder）

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他没想杀人，那就不是谋杀。

但考试真正问的是：恶意预谋（malice aforethought）里，想造成严重身体伤害本身就够了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的伤害有没有发生得更重或更轻」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干用棒球棍打脸、意图造成严重伤害，已经落入恶意预谋（malice aforethought），人死了就够定谋杀。

❌ 法律适用 | 构成要件错套

✕ A: 把 arson 想成“只要有火就行”，但题干没想烧房子。

❌ 事实误判 | 无法把戏当杀人

✕ C: 看到受惊死亡就硬塞 involuntary manslaughter，但题干没有刑事过失或违法行为。

❌ 概念混淆 | 故意要求错位

✕ D: 把 attempt 当成“结果危险就够”，但尝试犯必须有具体故意去做目标罪。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓主观心态，再看死亡结果；别被“没想杀”这句带偏。

考场速记

记住：谋杀（murder）不只看“想不想杀”，还看有没有想造成严重身体伤害（intent to inflict serious bodily injury）。

一句话速记：打得够狠、死人了，malice aforethought 可能已经成立。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was charged with battery in a jurisdiction that follows the "retreat" doctrine, and he pleaded self-defense. At his trial, the evidence established the following: A man and his wife were enjoying a drink at a tavern when the defendant entered and stood near the door. The wife whispered to her husband that the defendant was the man who had insulted her on the street the day before. The husband approached the defendant and said, "Get out of here, or I'll break your nose." The defendant said, "Don't come any closer, or I'll hurt you." When the husband raised his fists menacingly, the defendant pulled a can of pepper spray from his pocket, aimed it at the husband's face, and sprayed. The husband fell to the floor, writhing in pain.
Should the defendant be convicted?

choices.A: No, because he had no obligation to retreat before resorting to nondeadly force in self-defense.
choices.B: No, because there is no obligation to retreat when one is in an occupied structure.
choices.C: Yes, because he failed to retreat even though there was an opportunity available.
choices.D: Yes, because the husband did not threaten to use deadly force against him.

questions.explanation:
Self-defense
(justification for criminal conduct)
General requirements Duty to retreat
Nondeadly force
  • Actual & reasonable belief of imminent unlawful harm
  • Force reasonably necessary to prevent harm
  • Not initial aggressor
  • No duty to retreat
Deadly force
  • Actual & reasonable belief of imminent serious harm or death
  • Deadly force necessary to prevent harm
  • Not initial aggressor
  • Majority rule: No duty to retreat
  • Minority rule: Duty when safe retreat available unless inside one's home

Battery occurs when a person inflicts harmful or offensive contact on another. But a battery committed in self-defense is justified—and not subject to criminal liability—if the person:

  • actually and reasonably believed that force was necessary to protect against imminent unlawful harm
  • used reasonable force (ie, no more than necessary) to prevent such harm and
  • was not the initial aggressor—ie, did not provoke the altercation.

There is no duty to retreat before using nondeadly force in self-defense—even when one could do so safely (Choice C). But in the few jurisdictions that follow the retreat doctrine (as seen here), a person must retreat before using deadly force when that person is outside his/her home and can retreat with reasonable safety.

Here, the wife provoked the altercation when she told her husband that the defendant had insulted her the day before. The husband then approached the defendant, threatened to break his nose, and raised his fists menacingly. This caused the defendant to actually and reasonably believe that he was in danger of imminent unlawful harm, so he sprayed the husband's face with pepper spray. And since the defendant had no duty to retreat before using such nondeadly force in self-defense, he should not be convicted of battery.

(Choice B) There is no obligation to retreat before using nondeadly force in self-defense—no matter the location. And under the castle doctrine (minority rule), there is no obligation to retreat before using deadly force while in one's home—not any occupied structure (eg, the tavern).

(Choice D) The fact that the husband did not threaten to use deadly force means that the defendant could not have used deadly force in self-defense. But since he used nondeadly force (pepper spray), his actions were justified.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the retreat doctrine (minority rule), a person must retreat before using deadly force in self-defense if that person is outside his/her home and can do so with reasonable safety. But there is no duty to retreat before using nondeadly force in self-defense.
questions.zh-question:
一名被告在一个遵循“退让”原则的司法管辖区被控伤害罪（battery），他以正当防卫为由进行抗辩。在其审判中，证据证实了以下事实：一名男子和他的妻子正在一家酒馆喝酒，此时被告进入并站在门边。妻子对丈夫耳语说，被告就是前一天在街上侮辱她的那个男人。丈夫走近被告说：“滚出去，否则我打烂你的鼻子。”被告说：“别再靠近了，否则我会伤害你。”当丈夫威胁性地举起拳头时，被告从口袋里掏出一罐胡椒喷雾，对准丈夫的脸部进行喷射。丈夫倒在地上，痛苦地扭动。

被告是否应被定罪？

zh-choices.A: 不应定罪，因为他在为正当防卫而采取非致命武力之前，没有退让的义务。
zh-choices.B: 不应定罪，因为当一个人身处有人占用的建筑物内时，没有退让的义务。
zh-choices.C: 应定罪，因为尽管有机会退让，他却没有退让。
zh-choices.D: 应定罪，因为丈夫并未威胁对他使用致命武力。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Specific defenses

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：正当防卫（self-defense）里，面对的是非致命威胁时，非致命武力（nondeadly force）不需要先退。

三秒认题路径：

退让州 → 先看武力级别 → 这是非致命 → 不用先退 → 选无罪

核心法律规则

正当防卫（self-defense）的考场意思：你要先判断自己用的是非致命武力（nondeadly force）还是致命武力（deadly force）。本题里喷胡椒喷雾属于非致命武力，所以就算在retreat doctrine州，也没有先退义务。

只有在你要用致命武力时，才去看“能不能安全撤退”。而且这里还要求你不是先挑事的人，并且对方真的让你合理相信有马上到来的非法伤害。

核心判例： 题目考的是通行 MBE 规则：no duty to retreat before using nondeadly force；退让规则只卡致命武力。

思维导图

先问：他用的是不是 致命武力（deadly force）？
不是喷胡椒喷雾 = 非致命武力（nondeadly force）
卡死结论：no duty to retreat，先退这一步直接跳过
再看：是否有合理相信的马上非法伤害？有；是否是先挑事的人？题干没有。
因此：防卫成立 → 不应定罪
只有当你要用 致命武力（deadly force） 时，才继续问：能否安全撤退？
能安全撤退 → 先退
不能安全撤退 → 才可能继续用致命武力
本题最终按钮：选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题目既然写了 retreat doctrine，那只要有机会撤退就必须退。

但考试真正问的是：先看你用的是不是致命武力。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里是非致命武力，所以先退规则根本不启动。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里他用的是 pepper spray，属于非致命武力；因此即便在退让州，也没有先退义务，防卫成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ B: 把 occupied structure 当成本题门槛了，tavern 不是这里要考的关键。

❌ 法律适用 | 先退规则套错

✕ C: 把致命武力的先退要求硬搬到非致命武力上了。

❌ 事实误判 | 死亡威胁偷换

✕ D: 误以为对方没威胁 deadly force 就不能防卫；这里防的是非致命攻击。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定武力级别，再决定要不要看 retreat；非致命武力先直接排除撤退义务。

考场速记

记忆口诀：非致命不退，致命才看退。 题目一旦出现 pepper spray、拳头、推搡这类信号，先想“非致命”；只有真到致命武力，才去问能不能安全撤退。

question_analysis.skill_tested: distinguish deadly vs nondeadly force retreat obligations

reason.en: Identifies the minority jurisdiction rule requiring retreat before using deadly force.
reason.zh: 标识少数州要求在使用致命武力前撤退的规则。

reason.zh: 确立被告对紧迫非法伤害的合理相信，是正当防卫的必要条件。

reason.zh: 确定指控罪名，并提示适用的管辖规则（撤退原则）。

A.text: no obligation to retreat before resorting to nondeadly force

label.en: no retreat duty for nondeadly force
label.zh: 使用非致命武力无需撤退

B.text: no obligation to retreat when one is in an occupied structure

reason.en: Misstates the castle doctrine; it applies to one's home, not any occupied structure like a tavern.
reason.zh: 误述城堡原则；该原则适用于自己的住所，而非酒馆等任何有人占用的建筑。

C.text: failed to retreat even though there was an opportunity available

D.text: husband did not threaten to use deadly force against him

label.zh: 致命武力门槛与非致命回应无关

highlights.text: retreat" doctrine

reason.en: Signals that the jurisdiction requires retreat before deadly force, making the deadly/nondeadly distinction dispositive.
reason.zh: 表明该管辖区要求在使用致命武力前撤退，使致命/非致命的区分成为决定性因素。

highlights.text: pulled a can of pepper spray from his pocket, aimed it at the husband's face, and sprayed

reason.en: Establishes that pepper spray is nondeadly force, which carries no retreat obligation under any doctrine.
reason.zh: 确认胡椒喷雾属于非致命武力，在任何原则下均无撤退义务。

highlights.text: Get out of here, or I'll break your nose

reason.en: Confirms the defendant was not the initial aggressor, satisfying a self-defense element.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man who suffered from post-traumatic stress disorder became convinced that his neighbor was an evil demon. Truly believing that he needed to save the world from an evil demon, the man killed the neighbor. The man was charged with murder, and his defense attorney raised an insanity defense. During the trial, a psychiatrist testified that the man would not have killed the neighbor in the absence of his post-traumatic stress disorder and that the man did not think it was immoral to kill the neighbor because he believed the neighbor was an evil demon. The jurisdiction in which the court resides has adopted the M'Naghten test for insanity.
What is the man's strongest argument in support of an insanity defense?

choices.A: The man did not know the quality of the act he was performing.
choices.B: The man's acts were the product of a mental disease.
choices.C: The man did not know that his act was morally wrong.
choices.D: The man did not know the nature of the act he was performing.

questions.explanation:
Types of insanity defenses
M'Naghten
(majority rule)		 Mental illness prevented defendant from:
  • understanding nature or quality of the criminal act
    or
  • knowing that his/her actions were wrong
Irresistible impulse Mental illness prevented defendant from:
  • controlling actions or
  • conforming conduct to law
Durham/New Hampshire Defendant's criminal actions were product of mental illness
Model Penal Code Mental illness prevented defendant from:
  • appreciating criminality of act or
  • conforming conduct to law

This jurisdiction, like most jurisdictions, has adopted the M'Naghten test to determine if a criminal defendant was legally insane at the time of the criminal act. Under this test, a defendant is not guilty by reason of insanity if a mental illness prevented the defendant from:

  • understanding the nature and quality of the criminal act or
  • knowing that the defendant's actions were legally or morally wrong.

Here, the man understood the nature and quality of the act he was performing because he intentionally killed his neighbor under the mistaken belief that the neighbor was an evil demon (Choices A & D). However, the man's post-traumatic stress disorder (mental illness) caused him to form this mistaken belief and ultimately prevented him from knowing that his act was morally wrong. Therefore, this is the man's strongest argument in support of an insanity defense.

(Choice B) The fact that the man's acts were the product of a mental disease would, by itself, be sufficient to establish an insanity defense only if this jurisdiction had adopted the Durham test of insanity (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Under the M'Naghten test, a criminal defendant is not guilty by reason of insanity if a mental illness prevented the defendant from (1) understanding the nature and quality of the criminal act or (2) knowing that the defendant's actions were wrong.

📚 References
  • 21 Am. Jur. 2d Criminal Law § 50 (2023) (setting forth the M'Naghten test to determine insanity).
questions.zh-question:
一名患有创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的男子确信他的邻居是一个邪恶的恶魔。他坚信自己需要从邪恶的恶魔手中拯救世界，于是杀害了邻居。该男子被控谋杀，其辩护律师提出了精神错乱辩护（insanity defense）。审判期间，一名精神病医生作证称，如果该男子没有创伤后应激障碍，他就不会杀害邻居，并且该男子不认为杀害邻居是不道德的，因为他相信邻居是一个邪恶的恶魔。法院所在司法管辖区已采纳 M'Naghten 规则（M'Naghten test）作为精神错乱（insanity）的检验标准。
该男子支持精神错乱辩护（insanity defense）的最有力论点是什么？

zh-choices.A: 该男子不知道他所实施行为的性质（quality）。
zh-choices.B: 该男子的行为是精神疾病的产物。
zh-choices.C: 该男子不知道他的行为在道德上是错误的。
zh-choices.D: 该男子不知道他所实施行为的性质（nature）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Responsibility

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：M'Naghten 规则下，精神疾病能不能让被告主张自己不知道行为“错了”。

三秒认题路径：

精神疾病 → 疯癫抗辩 → M'Naghten → 不知错误 → 选 C

核心法律规则

M'Naghten test 的考场意思：如果精神疾病让被告 understand the nature and quality 失败，或者让他 know the act was wrong 失败，就能成立 insanity defense。这里的 wrong 不只看法律上错，也看道德上错。

所以这题不是问“他有没有精神病”，而是问“精神病有没有把他的错误认知打掉”。如果他只是把邻居看成恶魔，从而真的不觉得杀人是错的，就更贴近 M'Naghten 的第二条。

核心判例： M'Naghten 规则 - 只要精神疾病让被告不知道行为的性质，或不知道行为错误，就可能无罪认定。

思维导图

先看：这是在问 insanity defense 能不能成立吗？
是题干已给：post-traumatic stress disorder 让他把邻居当成恶魔。
再看：辖区采用哪一套？
M'Naghten 只问两件事：不懂行为性质，或不知道行为错。
本题卡点在哪？
卡死：他知道自己在杀人，但不觉得这是“错”
精神病把“邻居是恶魔”的认知放大，但更关键的是：他因此真的不知道这件事道德上是错的。
结论：选 C，did not know that his act was morally wrong。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然他把人当成恶魔，那是不是就不知道自己在做什么、甚至不知道行为的性质？

但考试真正问的是：他有没有因为精神疾病而不知道这件事“错”。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里真正打赢抗辩的，不是“他很疯狂”，而是“他不觉得杀人是错的”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里精神科医生已经说他 不认为杀人是 immoral，这正好打中 M'Naghten 的“知道行为错误”要件，所以 C 最强。

❌ 概念混淆 | 性质认知误判

✕ A: 把“当成恶魔”偷换成不知道 quality，其实他知道自己在杀人。

❌ 法律适用 | 他州规则套错

✕ B: “产物于精神病”是 Durham 口径，不是本题的 M'Naghten。

❌ 事实误判 | 认知层级偷换

✕ D: 他不是没看出自己在做什么，而是觉得自己在救世界。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定精神病测试名称，再只盯“知道错没错”这一个门槛。

考场速记

记忆口诀：M'Naghten 只看两件事，nature and quality 或 wrong；本题抓住“他不觉得杀人是错的”，通常就能秒选 C。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A state statute provides: "The sale of an alcoholic beverage to any person under the age of 21 is a misdemeanor." A woman who was 20 years old, but who looked older and who had a very convincing fake driver's license indicating that she was 24, entered a convenience store, picked up a six-pack of beer, and placed the beer on the counter. The store clerk, after examining the driver's license, rang up the purchase. Both the clerk and the store owner were charged with violating the state statute. At trial, the court found both the clerk and store owner guilty.
What standard of liability must the court have interpreted the statute to impose?

choices.A: Strict liability only.
choices.B: Vicarious liability only.
choices.C: Both strict and vicarious liability.
choices.D: Either strict or vicarious liability.

questions.explanation:
Types of mens rea

Specific intent
(all attempted crimes)
General intent
(battery, rape)
Strict liability
(sale to minor, statutory rape)
Intentional Purposely or knowingly causes
particular result
Reckless Consciously disregards substantial &
unjustifiable risk
Criminally Negligent Grossly deviates from
standard of reasonable care
No mens rea No showing of
fault required

Most crimes require proof that a person committed a particular act (actus reus) with a particular state of mind (mens rea). But strict liability crimes have no mens rea requirement. This means that proof of the actus reus alone is sufficient to support a conviction. And persons can be directly liable for the strict liability crime if they commit the actus reus themselves OR vicariously liable if their agent (often an employee) does so.

Here, the clerk and store owner were convicted of violating the state statute after the clerk sold beer to a woman who was under 21 years of age (actus reus). But the clerk did not do so knowingly, or even negligently, since the woman looked older and the clerk examined her driver's license (no mens rea). Therefore, the court must have interpreted the statute as imposing strict liability to convict the clerk.

And since the store owner did not personally complete the sale, the court must have construed the statute as authorizing vicarious liability to convict the store owner for the sale by the clerk (the owner's agent) (Choices A, B, & D).

📌 Educational Objective

Strict liability crimes require a particular actus reus—but not a particular mens rea. And persons can be (1) directly liable for such crimes if they commit the actus reus themselves or (2) vicariously liable if their agent does so.
questions.zh-question:
某州法规规定：“向任何未满21岁的人出售酒精饮料属于轻罪。”一名20岁的女子，但看起来比实际年龄大，并持有一张非常逼真的伪造驾照，显示她24岁。她进入一家便利店，拿起一提六瓶装的啤酒，并将其放在柜台上。店员在检查了驾照后，为她结了账。店员和店主均被指控违反该州法规。在审判中，法院裁定店员和店主均有罪。

法院必须将该法规解释为施加了何种责任标准？

zh-choices.A: 仅严格责任。
zh-choices.B: 仅替代责任。
zh-choices.C: 严格责任和替代责任兼有。
zh-choices.D: 严格责任或替代责任之一。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Mens Rea- State of Mind

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：无 mens rea 的 严格责任（strict liability），以及店员卖出时，店主能否因雇员行为被追成 替代责任（vicarious liability）。

三秒认题路径：

未成年买酒 → 无主观心态 → 严格责任 → 员工代卖 → 店主连坐

核心法律规则

一般犯罪要同时看 行为（actus reus） 和 主观心态（mens rea）；但 严格责任（strict liability） 只要做了禁止的行为就够了，考试意思：不用再证明他“知道”或“应当知道”。

如果法律把“卖给 21 岁以下的人”写成严格责任，店员即使被假证骗了，照样可能被定罪；这说明法院把这条法规定成了“只看有没有卖出去”，不看心里有没有错。

再往下看，店主没有亲自收钱也能被判，是因为法院还把这条法理解成允许对雇员的销售行为追到老板身上，也就是 替代责任（vicarious liability）。

核心判例： 本题对应的判法逻辑与 public welfare offense 一致：若法规只盯行为本身，法院可用严格责任；若违法动作由员工完成，老板可被按代理关系追责。

思维导图

先问：这条法规要不要 mens rea？
YES：要证明知道、故意、鲁莽或过失，才谈得上主观心态。
NO：只看有没有完成“卖给未满 21 岁的人”这个动作。
再问：谁做了卖酒这个动作？
店员：亲自完成交易 → 可直接适用严格责任。
假证、看起来更老，只能挡 mens rea；这里 mens rea 本来就不重要。
店主：没亲自收钱，但员工是他的代理人 → 可用替代责任追到老板。
最后结论
法院若要把两个人都判有罪，就必须把法规读成：对店员是严格责任，对店主是替代责任。
所以答案锁定：C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：店员明明被假证骗了，应该没罪，店主也不该背锅。

但考试真正问的是：这条州法是不是压根就不要 mens rea，只要卖给未满 21 岁的人就够了；如果是，店员先中招，店主再因雇员售酒被连带追责。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题最容易把“有无善意”误当成“有无构成要件”，但这里善意只能打在一般故意犯上，打不掉严格责任。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里店员把酒卖给 未满 21 岁 的人，说明法院把这条法读成了对店员用 严格责任（strict liability），再对店主按雇员售卖追成 替代责任（vicarious liability）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 只盯 no mens rea，却漏了店主还得靠替代责任。

❌ 法律适用 | 主体范围误判

✕ B: 把责任全推给老板，忘了店员本人也能直接因严格责任被判。

❌ 事实误判 | 双重条件偷换

✕ D: 想成“二选一”，但本题两种责任是可以一起成立的。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“是否需要 mens rea”，再看“行为人本人”与“雇主”能否分别落进严格责任和替代责任。

考场速记

记住一句：严格责任（strict liability） 先看行为，后看心态；如果是员工完成违法动作，老板再看 替代责任（vicarious liability）。这题的口袋口诀就是：“先看卖没卖，再看谁替谁卖。”

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Plagued by neighborhood youths who had been stealing lawn furniture from his backyard, a man remained awake nightly watching for them. One evening the man heard noises in his backyard. He yelled out, warning intruders to leave. Receiving no answer, he fired a shotgun filled with nonlethal buckshot into bushes along his back fence, where he believed the intruders might be hiding. A six-year-old boy was hiding in the bushes and was struck in the eye by some of the pellets, causing loss of sight. The man is charged with second-degree assault, which is defined in the jurisdiction as "maliciously causing serious physical injury to another."
What verdict should the jury render at the man's trial?

choices.A: Guilty, because the man recklessly caused serious physical injury.
choices.B: Guilty, because there is no privilege to use force against a person who is too young to be criminally responsible.
choices.C: Not guilty, because the child was trespassing and the man was using what he believed was nondeadly force.
choices.D: Not guilty, because the man did not intend to kill or to cause serious physical injury.

questions.explanation:
Justifications for criminal acts
Necessity
  • Reasonable belief that conduct was necessary to avoid imminent & substantial harm
  • No reasonable legal alternative
  • Harm caused < harm avoided
Self-defense
  • Actual & reasonable belief that harm is imminent
  • Reasonable force used to prevent harm
  • Not initial aggressor
Defense of others
  • Actual & reasonable belief that force is necessary to protect victim from imminent harm
  • Reasonable force used to protect victim
Defense of property
  • Force reasonably necessary to prevent imminent & unlawful interference with possessed property
  • Nondeadly force used
Law enforcement
  • Prevent imminent crime
  • Make lawful arrest or
  • Prevent suspect's escape from custody
Resisting arrest
  • Reasonable force permitted to resist unlawful arrest or arrest by unknown police officer

This jurisdiction defines second-degree assault as maliciously causing serious physical injury to another. Malice requires proof of either:

  • intent – conscious desire or practical certainty that one's act will cause a particular result or
  • recklessness – conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk of harm.

Here, the man did not intend to kill or cause serious injury when he fired a shotgun filled with nonlethal buckshot into the bushes where he believed intruders might be hiding (Choice D). But he recklessly (ie, maliciously) disregarded the substantial and unjustifiable risk that this would cause serious physical injury. And since some of the pellets struck the boy in the eye, causing loss of sight, the man committed second-degree assault.

However, an assault committed in defense of property may be justified if the person (1) reasonably believed that property in his/her possession was in danger of imminent unlawful interference (eg, trespass) and (2) used reasonable, nondeadly force to prevent such interference. Here, although the boy was trespassing and the man believed he was using nondeadly force, it was unreasonable to fire a shotgun into the bushes (Choice C). As a result, the man's use of force was not justified and he should be found guilty of second-degree assault.

(Choice B) The privilege to use force against another, whether in defense of one's self or property, does not turn on that person's age. But the person's age and characteristics may be considered in determining whether the use of force was reasonable.

📌 Educational Objective

An assault committed in defense of property may be justified if the person (1) reasonably believed that property in his/her possession was in danger of imminent unlawful interference and (2) used reasonable, nondeadly force to prevent such interference.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子因其后院的草坪家具屡遭附近青少年偷窃而深受其扰，遂夜夜保持清醒，守候窃贼。一天晚上，该男子听到后院有响动。他大声喊叫，警告入侵者离开。在没有得到任何回应后，他向后院围栏边的灌木丛开了一枪，他认为入侵者可能藏在那里。枪中装的是非致命性的鹿弹。一名六岁的男孩正藏在灌木丛中，被一些弹丸击中眼睛，导致失明。该男子被控二级攻击罪 (second-degree assault)，该司法管辖区将其定义为“恶意对他人造成严重身体伤害”。

在该男子的审判中，陪审团应作出何种裁决？

zh-choices.A: 有罪，因为该男子鲁莽地造成了严重的身体伤害。
zh-choices.B: 有罪，因为对一个因年龄太小而无刑事责任能力的人使用武力，并不享有特权。
zh-choices.C: 无罪，因为该儿童正在非法侵入，而该男子使用的是他认为是'非致命性'的武力。
zh-choices.D: 无罪，因为该男子无意杀人或造成严重身体伤害。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Specific defenses

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：防卫财产（defense of property）能不能挡住鲁莽（recklessness）造成的严重伤害；答案是不能，因为用了过度危险的火力。

三秒认题路径：

看见夜里开枪 → 先想财产防卫 → 再看是否合理 → 枪打灌木太险 → 仍是有罪

核心法律规则

这里的罪名是二级攻击，题目要求的是“恶意”造成严重身体伤害。恶意（malice）在考场里就是两条路：要么你故意（intent）想造成那个结果，要么你鲁莽（recklessness）地无视了明显而重大、而且不该忽视的伤害风险。

本题里，男人不是为了杀人或必然重伤才开枪，所以不是故意；但他明知灌木里可能有人，还把装着霰弹的猎枪往里打，这就是鲁莽。只要伤害结果真的发生，recklessly 造成严重伤害，就够成立二级攻击。

至于防卫财产（defense of property），它只允许你在合理相信财产正面临迫近的非法干扰时，使用合理且非致命（reasonable, nondeadly）的力量；这题里向灌木里开枪太危险，已经超过“非致命”的安全边界，所以特权挡不住刑责。

核心判例： 本题不靠具体判例名，靠的是一般 MBE 规则：财产防卫不能用明显过度的危险手段，且鲁莽造成重伤仍可构成恶意攻击。

思维导图

先看有没有“正当化特权”可以挡罪：防卫财产？
条件1是否合理相信财产正遭受迫近的非法干扰（imminent unlawful interference）？
有可能满足：邻居小孩确实在偷东西，属于 trespass 语境。
条件2是否用了合理、非致命（reasonable, nondeadly）的力量？
这里直接卡死：对着灌木开霰弹枪，风险太高，不算合理非致命。
特权失败后，再回到罪名：是否maliciously 造成严重身体伤害？
不是一定要想杀人；鲁莽（recklessness）地无视重大伤害风险，也够“恶意”。
结论：不能靠防卫财产免责，结果是 A 正确。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：孩子在偷东西，而且男人只想用“非致命”方式赶人，应该能算防卫财产。

但考试真正问的是：你用的手段是不是合理且非致命，不是你主观上有没有想杀人。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这题换成刑法语言，就是看你有没有超出财产防卫的安全边界。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干关键事实是他向灌木里开枪，明知有人可能躲着，却仍制造了严重伤害风险；这正是recklessly caused serious physical injury，所以构成二级攻击。

❌ 概念混淆 | 年龄无关误判

✕ B: 把“太小就不能被打”想成免责点，too young 不是这里的门槛。

❌ 法律适用 | 非致命误区

✕ C: 只盯着“非致命”四个字，忽略了开枪本身已经不合理。

❌ 事实误判 | 主观意图偷换

✕ D: 没想杀人，不等于没recklessness。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓罪名里的“恶意”，再看防卫财产是否被“合理、非致命”这道门卡住。

考场速记

记住：防卫财产能挡的是“合理的非致命力量”，挡不住“明知有重大风险还开枪”。看到有人主张只是“没想杀人”，先问自己：有没有鲁莽（recklessness）？有的话，还是可能有罪。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A kidnapping statute in State A makes it a crime for a person, including a parent, to "take a child from the custody of his custodial parent, knowing he has no privilege to do so." After a bitter court battle, a woman and man were divorced, and the woman was given custody of their daughter.
The man later moved to State B, where he brought an action to obtain custody of the daughter. A local judge awarded him custody. His attorney incorrectly advised him that, under this award, he was entitled to take the daughter away from the woman. The man drove to State A, picked the daughter up at her preschool, and took her back to State B with him. He was indicted for kidnapping in State A, extradited from State B, and tried.
At trial, he testified that he had relied on his attorney's advice in taking the daughter, and that at the time he believed his conduct was not illegal.
If the jury believes the man's testimony, what should be its finding?

choices.A: Acquitted, because he acted on the advice of an attorney.
choices.B: Acquitted, because he lacked a necessary mental element of the crime.
choices.C: Convicted, because reliance on an attorney's advice is not a defense.
choices.D: Convicted, provided a reasonable person would have known that the attorney's advice was erroneous.

questions.explanation:
Mistake of law v. Mistake of fact
Definition Applicability
Mistake of law Defendant mistakenly believes conduct not prohibited by law
  • No defense unless:
    • Law prohibiting conduct was unavailable
    • Defendant reasonably relied on invalid law
    • Mistake negates mens rea*
Mistake of
fact		 Defendant is mistaken as to a matter of fact
  • When mistake negates mens rea:
    • Specific intent – defense if honest mistake
    • General intent & malice – defense if honest & reasonable mistake
    • Strict liability – no defense
*Mens rea – state of mind necessary to be guilty of criminal offense.

A defendant's mistaken belief that his/her conduct was not prohibited by law (i.e., mistake of law) is rarely a defense to criminal liability. But it is a valid defense when it negates the required mens rea (i.e., mental state) for the crime. And though a client's reliance on erroneous legal advice from an attorney does not itself give rise to mistake of law as an affirmative defense, it may negate the required intent or other mental state for a material element of the crime.

Here, State A's kidnapping statute makes it a crime for any person to take a child from his/her custodial parent, knowing that he/she has no privilege to do so. And the man did take the daughter away from the woman (her custodial parent) in State A. However, the man's attorney had incorrectly advised the man that he was legally entitled to take the daughter. As a result, the man's mistake of law negates the necessary mental element of the crime (i.e., the man did not know that he had no privilege to take the daughter), and he should be acquitted.

(Choices A, C & D) Erroneous legal advice from an attorney is not itself a valid defense—regardless of whether a reasonable person would have known that the advice was erroneous or relied on it. But it may negate the required mental state for the crime (as seen here). In that case, a mistake-of-law defense is appropriate.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant's mistaken belief that his/her conduct was not prohibited by law (i.e., mistake of law) is a defense to a crime when it negates the required mens rea. And though a client's reliance on erroneous legal advice does not give rise to a mistake-of-law defense, it may negate the required mental state for a material element of the crime.

在一场激烈的法庭斗争后，一名女子和一名男子离婚，女子获得了他们女儿的监护权。

该男子后来搬到B州，并在那里提起诉讼以获得女儿的监护权。当地一名法官将监护权判给了他。他的律师错误地告知他，根据这项判决，他有权将女儿从女子身边带走。该男子开车前往A州，从女儿的幼儿园接走她，并把她带回了B州。他在A州因绑架罪被起诉，从B州被引渡，并接受审判。

在审判中，他作证称，他在带走女儿时是依据其律师的建议行事，并且当时他相信自己的行为并非违法。

如果陪审团相信该男子的证词，应作出何种裁定？

zh-choices.A: 无罪，因为他根据律师的建议行事。
zh-choices.B: 无罪，因为他缺乏该罪行必要的犯罪意图要素。
zh-choices.C: 有罪，因为信赖律师的建议不构成抗辩理由。
zh-choices.D: 有罪，前提是一个理性人本应知道该律师的建议是错误的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - State of mind

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：错误理解法律（mistake of law） 什么时候能让被告少了犯罪所需的心理状态（mens rea），从而无罪。

三秒认题路径：

律师误导 → 以为合法 → 少了故意 → 触发 mens rea 问题 → 选无罪

核心法律规则

一般来说，错误理解法律（mistake of law） 不能单独当刑事抗辩；但如果它直接让被告没有犯罪法条要求的主观罪过（mens rea），就可能无罪。换句话说，考试不只看你“知不知道法律”，还要看法条是不是要求你明知自己没权利这么做。

这里法条要求被告知道自己没有权利把孩子带走，所以如果他真的相信自己有权，mens rea 就断了。律师错误法律意见（erroneous legal advice） 本身不是万能抗辩，但它可以成为“我当时根本不知自己无权”的证据。

核心判例： 本题不靠背具体案名，靠的是考试规则：律师错误法律意见 不能独立洗白行为，但可以击穿法条要求的心理状态。

思维导图

被告是否“知道自己没有权利”带走孩子？
YES：法条所需的 mens rea 成立 → 可定罪。
NO：他真的相信律师说法，错误理解法律（mistake of law） 直接打掉“明知无权”这个要件。
卡死点：不是问“律师意见可不可以直接当抗辩”，而是问它有没有让被告少了法条要求的心理状态。
结果：少了必要心理状态 → 选 B，无罪。
记法：“先看法条要不要 know，再看被告有没有真的 know。”

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然他是听了律师的话，那就可以直接用“律师建议”当抗辩。

但考试真正问的是：这句话有没有让他在当时缺少法条要求的明知无权，而不是律师意见本身能不能自动免责。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干关键点是他真的以为自己有权带走孩子，这正好打掉法条要求的“知道自己无权”，所以应无罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 律师抗辩误判

✕ A: 把“听律师的话”误当成自动免责。

❌ 法律适用 | 绝对禁止误判

✕ C: 看到 not a defense 就停住了，忽略它还能打掉 mens rea。

❌ 事实误判 | 合理人标准误判

✕ D: 题目问的是他主观是否知道，不是看旁人会不会觉得律师错了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯法条写的是不是“知道无权”，再判断被告的错误理解有没有把这个心理状态打掉。

考场速记

记住这句：错把法律当事实不一定能免责，但如果它刚好打掉了法条要求的心理状态，就可能无罪。

这类题先问一句：法条要不要被告“知道/明知”某个法律后果？要的话，就抓住这个 mens rea 点，不要被“律师说错了”四个字带跑。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A husband and wife took their 12-year-old son to a political rally in an auditorium to hear a controversial United States senator speak. The speaker was late, and the wife stepped outside the auditorium to smoke a cigarette. While there, she saw a man placing what she believed to be a bomb against the back wall of the auditorium. She went back inside and told her husband what she had seen. Without alerting anyone, they took their son and left. Some 20 minutes later, the bomb exploded, killing eight persons and injuring 50.
In the jurisdiction, murder in the first degree is defined as an intentional homicide committed with premeditation and deliberation; murder in the second degree is defined as all other murder at common law; and manslaughter is defined as either a homicide in the heat of passion arising from adequate provocation or a homicide caused by gross negligence or reckless indifference to consequence.
As to the deaths of the eight persons, what crime, if any, did the wife commit?

choices.A: Manslaughter.
choices.B: Murder in the first degree.
choices.C: Murder in the second degree.
choices.D: No crime.

questions.explanation:
To commit criminal homicide, a person must unlawfully kill another (actus reus) with the requisite mental state (mens rea). Criminal liability typically stems from a voluntary act—an overt movement over which the defendant has conscious control (eg, deliberately pulling a gun's trigger). But criminal liability can also arise from a failure to act (ie, omission) if the defendant had a legal duty to act and could have reasonably done so. A legal duty to act can arise under any of the following circumstances:

  • The defendant and the victim are in a special relationship (eg, parent/child, spouses).
  • The defendant assumed the victim's care by rendering aid.
  • The defendant's conduct created the risk of harm to the victim.
  • A statute imposes a duty.
  • A contract imposes a duty.

Here, the wife saw a man place what appeared to be a bomb in the auditorium. She told her husband, and they left with their son. The bomb went off shortly thereafter and killed eight people. Although the wife had a legal duty to protect her husband and son from the bomb based on their special relationship, she had no legal duty to warn anyone else. Therefore, she did not commit any degree of criminal homicide—first-degree murder, second-degree murder, or manslaughter (Choices A, B, & C).

📌 Educational Objective

A person is not criminally liable for failing to act unless he/she had a legal duty to do so. A legal duty can be based on (1) a special relationship, (2) assumption of care, (3) creation of the risk of harm, (4) a statute, or (5) a contract.
questions.zh-question:
一对夫妻带着他们12岁的儿子去一个礼堂参加政治集会，聆听一位有争议的美国参议员的演讲。演讲者迟到了，妻子走出礼堂去抽烟。在外面时，她看到一名男子将她认为是炸弹的东西放在礼堂的后墙上。她回到礼堂内，将所见之事告诉了丈夫。他们没有警告任何人，就带着儿子离开了。大约20分钟后，炸弹爆炸，造成8人死亡，50人受伤。

在该司法管辖区，一级谋杀罪（murder in the first degree）的定义是经过预谋和深思熟虑后实施的故意杀人行为；二级谋杀罪（murder in the second degree）的定义是普通法（common law）上的所有其他谋杀行为；而过失杀人罪（manslaughter）的定义是因充分的挑衅而一时激愤下实施的杀人行为，或因重大过失或对后果鲁莽漠视而造成的杀人行为。

就这八人的死亡而言，该妻子犯了什么罪行（如有）？

zh-choices.A: 过失杀人罪。
zh-choices.B: 一级谋杀罪。
zh-choices.C: 二级谋杀罪。
zh-choices.D: 未构成犯罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: General Principles - Actus Reus- Acts and Omissions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：不作为（omission）能不能当成杀人罪的行为基础，关键看她有没有对他人承担法定义务。

三秒认题路径：

先问不作为 → 再找义务 → 仅护家人 → 他人无义务 → 选无罪

核心法律规则

只记这一组规则

刑事责任通常要有自愿行为（voluntary act），也就是可控的外在动作；不作为（omission）只有在被告对某人负有法定义务时，才可能变成可罚的行为基础。

法定义务（legal duty）的常见来源有五个：特殊关系、主动救助后接管照顾、自己制造风险、法规命令、合同义务。考场意思：没义务，就算你“看见了、知道了、走开了”，通常也不会因为没救陌生人而被判谋杀或过失杀人。

核心判例： Common law 规则下的标准思路：只有对有义务保护的人不救，才可能把“不作为”算进犯罪行为；对旁观陌生人通常没有一般救助义务。

思维导图

先看：她是“做了什么”还是“没做什么”？
不是主动杀人
她只是听到消息后离开，没有开枪、下毒、投弹等 voluntary act。
改问不作为能不能罚
只有有 legal duty，不救才会变成刑法上的“行为”。
这题的义务范围
她对丈夫和儿子有 special relationship 的义务；但对会场里的其他人，没有一般警告义务。
卡死点：对八名死者没有法定义务，所以 effectively reviewable 之外的救济不是问题；这里直接是“无犯罪行为基础”。
结论
不能把她对陌生人的沉默，算成 murder 或 manslaughter 的 actus reus。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她明明看见了“炸弹”，还带着家人离开，太冷漠了，应该算犯罪。

但考试真正问的是：她对这八名受害人有没有法定义务（legal duty）去警告或救助。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干只显示她对丈夫和儿子有照顾义务，没有对八名死者的 法定义务；所以她的不作为不能成立任何一级 homicide。

❌ 概念混淆 | 义务范围偷换

✕ A: 把对家人的义务偷换成对所有人的义务了。

❌ 法律适用 | 故意杀人硬套

✕ B: 看到爆炸死亡就硬套一级谋杀，漏了行为基础。

❌ 事实误判 | 风险来源错认

✕ C: 以为她制造了危险，其实炸弹不是她放的。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓是否存在可罚的不作为，再把法定义务限定在题干真正给出的关系里。

考场速记

记忆口诀：不作为先找义务，没义务就没 actus reus；五个来源记成“亲、救、险、法、约”。

reason.en: Signals a possible legal duty arising from relationship.
reason.zh: 提示可能因关系而产生法定义务。

reason.en: Raises a potential duty to protect a child.
reason.zh: 提示对未成年子女可能存在保护义务。

reason.en: Tests whether silence can create homicide liability.
reason.zh: 考查沉默是否会构成杀人责任。
